consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning treats valley as a place or season of trial, suffering, hardship, grief, spiritual darkness or low points (most often from Ps 23:4), contrasted with mountaintop experiences of nearness or victory; common alternatives include divine judgment/decision, humility/lowliness that God exalts, restoration from desolation, and (minority) fertility/blessing.
book_summary: Valley is the low and humbled passage between mountain-kingdoms: the Way of descent, service, and obedience even unto death by which one leaves one rule and ascends another; a valley lifted or filled pictures resurrection, exaltation, and preparation of the Way into the Mountain of God (opposite: Mountain).
consensus_core_identification: place/season of trial, suffering, hardship or spiritual low point
book_core_identification: low humbled passage/Way of descent-service-obedience unto death between mountain-kingdoms (rule transition); lifted valley as resurrection/exaltation
boundary_disagreement: Book narrows the broad experiential category of any hardship/low point to the specific transitional path of kenotic descent between opposing mountain-kingdoms and re-centers lifted valleys on resurrection/exaltation/preparation of the Way; it thereby de-emphasizes or sidelines general trial seasons, judgment valleys, and fertility motifs that consensus admits.
material_contradiction: None; the book explicitly notes the common trial/death-versus-mountaintop reading and retains lowliness, death, and exaltation without denying them.
rationale: Both share the low/humbled and death-to-exaltation imagery (Isa 40/Luke 3, Ezek 37, Phil 2). The book keeps that referent but materially tightens its extension and conditions into a kingdom-transition “Way,” adding the 1 Sam 17 valley-between-mountains frame and the leave-one-rule/ascend-another dynamic. This is boundary refinement, not core replacement or novelty; consensus already lists humility-exaltation as a common alternative.
strongest_objection: The distinctive ‘mountain-kingdoms’ / rule-transition framing and omission of the dominant Ps 23:4 trial text make the entry feel more inventive than the cited verses strictly require.
